name: app-shell
title: App shell
summary: Frames a page or an app: places a header, the navigation, the main content, an aside and a footer, decides from the window's width how each of them is shown, and lets a keyboard reach the content in one step; it draws the frame and none of what stands in it.

anatomy.description: The frame itself: the whole window (or the whole page), filled with the product's surface color. It carries no state and takes no input.

A Link the product gives ("Skip to content") that the shell keeps out of sight until the keyboard reaches it, then shows in a small raised box at the top start corner of the window. The first thing the keyboard reaches; following it moves focus to the main region.
A strip across the top of the frame, above the header, for a notice that concerns the whole product (a callout the product places there: an outage, a new version, a page that is not translated).
The region across the top that names the product or the screen and holds its search and its actions: the product's app bar. The page's banner landmark.

An icon-only Button the product puts in its header and marks as the shell's — or, in a frame whose header region is empty, gives in the menu-button slot, where it stands alone in the header's place and stays at the top of the window while the page scrolls, with no band around it (APS-34). The shell shows it in every window class (with menuButtonPlacement drawer, only while the navigation has no place in the layout). It opens and closes the navigation over the content, and where the navigation stands beside the content shows, hides or collapses it.

The region at the start edge that holds the product's destinations: a navigation drawer. Beside the main content in a wide window, its column of icons in a narrower one, and over the content in a narrow one — below the header, which stays in view and usable.
The content the page is for, and the page's one main landmark. Inset from the frame by a gutter and, by default, no wider than a readable width.

Content that supports the main content: an outline of the page, details of the selected thing, related links. Beside the main content at the end edge in a wide window, above or below it in a narrower one. A complementary landmark.

The region at the end of the page for what belongs to the whole site: its links, its legal line, its language and theme controls. The page's content-information landmark. Shown while the product fills it and has not hidden it (footerHidden).
The place at the bottom edge for a navigation bar, shown only in a narrow window, for a product whose three to five top-level destinations stay in reach of the thumb.

The hairline the shell draws between two regions that touch, where the system parts things with a line and the region's own component draws none: above the footer, and at the edge of an aside that is not a side sheet.

props.name: scroll
props.description: What scrolls. page: the whole page scrolls in the window, the header stays at the top (headerPosition) and the navigation and the aside stay in view beside the content; the default, because it is what find-in-page, anchors, the back button's return to where the reader was, and a phone browser's collapsing bars are built for. main: the frame is exactly as tall as the window and only the main region scrolls inside it, for an app whose panes scroll apart from each other (a mail client, an editor).

props.name: headerPosition
props.description: Whether the header stays at the top of the window while the page scrolls (sticky) or scrolls away with it (static: an article that should have the whole window). Ignored while scroll is main, where the header never moves.

props.name: mainWidth
props.description: contained: the main region's content is no wider than the shell's readable width and is centred in the room the region has, for pages that are read. full: it takes all the room inside the gutters, for a table, a board, an editor.

props.name: asideOrder
props.description: Where the aside stands in reading and focus order, and so where it is drawn when it is not beside the main content. after: it follows the main content and is drawn below it (related links, details). before: it precedes the main content and is drawn above it (an outline of the page, which is of use only before the page is read). Beside the main content it is drawn at the end edge either way.

props.name: footerHidden
props.description: Whether the footer is left out of the frame although the product fills it: a screen that is a task rather than a page of the site (a checkout, a sign-in, an editor, a full-window map) keeps the site's footer markup and shows none. While true the footer takes no space, draws no line, is no landmark and has no stop in focus order, exactly as an empty footer region. The footer is shown only while the product fills the footer slot and this is false: footerHidden never makes a footer of an unfilled slot.

props.name: separation
props.description: How regions that touch are told apart. auto takes the design system's choice through comp.app-shell.separation; divider draws the one hairline; gap draws nothing and leaves the regions' own spaces. It concerns only the edges the shell draws: a component in a region that has an edge of its own (an app bar, a navigation drawer, a side sheet) keeps it.

props.name: navigationOpen
props.description: Whether the navigation is presented over the content — below the header — while it has no place of its own in the layout (or only its column). The menu button asks for true and, while it is true, for false; closing the navigation makes it false, and so does the window becoming wide enough for the navigation to stand beside the content. A change between the two narrower classes keeps it. Ignored while the navigation stands beside the content.

props.name: menuButtonPlacement
props.description: Where the one control that shows and hides the navigation lives. header: the menu button in the header, in every window class — it opens and closes the navigation over the content where the navigation has no place (or only its column), and where it stands beside the content shows, hides or collapses it; the default. drawer: the navigation drawer's own menu button (its first header button) collapses and expands it where it has a place, and the header's menu button is shown only where the navigation has none. WHILE the header region is empty the menu button of the menu-button slot is shown as drawer shows it, whatever this says (APS-34).

props.name: asideLabel
props.description: Names the aside for assistive technology, in the product's language ("On this page"). Required where the aside is filled and what it holds does not name itself (a side sheet is named by its headline).

items.name: menu-button
items.summary: The one icon-only Button in the header — or, while the header region is empty, in the menu-button slot — that opens the navigation: a Button of the text variant and the medium size with the menu glyph and no label, unless the product sets otherwise, which the shell shows by menuButtonPlacement and does not restyle.

props.name: label
props.description: Its accessible name ("Menu"), as the Button's label. Required.

slots.name: icon
slots.description: Its glyph, as the Button's icon slot. A fixture item's content is this glyph.

events.name: click
events.description: The button was activated, as the Button's click. The shell answers it itself (APS-7); a product need not.

slots.name: default
slots.description: The main region: the page's content. A fixture's content string is plain text.

slots.name: skip-link
slots.description: The skip link: a standalone Link whose destination is the main region, with the product's words ("Skip to content"). More than one may be given ("Skip to navigation"); each is shown while it has focus.

slots.name: announcement
slots.description: The notice above the header: a callout the product places, drawn across the frame's width.

slots.name: header
slots.description: The header: the product's app bar, with its search and its actions, and the menu button in its navigation slot.

slots.name: menu-button
slots.description: The menu button of a frame whose header region is empty: the menu-button item, which the shell places alone in the header's place and keeps at the top of the window (APS-34). Not shown while the header region holds something, where the menu button belongs in the header. A fixture gives it as its menu-button item, not as a string.

slots.name: navigation
slots.description: The navigation: a navigation drawer, which draws each of the three presentations itself. Anything else is placed beside the content where the navigation has a place and is not shown where it has none.

slots.name: aside
slots.description: The aside: the product's supporting content, or a side sheet.

slots.name: footer
slots.description: The footer: the product's own layout of links, a legal line and controls. The shell gives it a place and an inset and no anatomy.

slots.name: navigation-bar
slots.description: A navigation bar for the bottom edge of a narrow window.

events.name: windowClassChange
events.description: The shell decided the window's class for the first time, or the window's width changed it; carries compact, medium or expanded. A product switches what follows the class and has no setting of its own for it: a search's presentation, a side sheet's variant, the form of an outline.

events.name: navigationOpenChange
events.description: The navigation asks to be presented over the content or to be put away: the menu button was activated while it was closed (true), or the open navigation closed — by its scrim, Escape, the platform's back, a drag, a destination that was activated, the menu button, or the window becoming wide enough for the navigation to stand beside the content (false). Carries the value asked for.

behavior.text: THE app shell SHALL fill the window with comp.app-shell.container.color, hand everything it holds comp.app-shell.content.color as the platform's inherited foreground, and place its regions in this order: the announcement across the top; the header across the top below it (WHILE the header region is empty, the menu button of the menu-button slot alone in its place, APS-34); then a row that holds the navigation at the start edge, the main region, and the aside at the end edge; the footer across the bottom of the page; and the navigation bar across the bottom edge of the window. A region that holds nothing, and the footer WHILE footerHidden is true (APS-31), SHALL take no space, draw nothing and add no landmark, and the regions beside it SHALL take its room. THE app shell SHALL draw no elevation and no corner of its own.

THE app shell SHALL give the window one of three classes by its width alone: compact WHILE the window is narrower than comp.app-shell.breakpoint.medium, medium WHILE it is at least that wide and narrower than comp.app-shell.breakpoint.expanded, and expanded WHILE it is at least comp.app-shell.breakpoint.expanded wide. It SHALL derive the class anew whenever the width changes, SHALL never store it, and SHALL NOT read the window's height, the device, the pointer or the orientation for it. WHERE the platform measures a window in a unit that grows with the reader's text size (the web's rem) the two widths SHALL be compared in that unit, so that enlarged text moves the frame to a narrower class before its columns become too narrow to read.
behavior.verify: Under the default system the two widths are 600 and 1024. Fixtures whose id begins with `expanded` are drawn in a window 1280 wide and 800 high, those that begin with `medium` in one 800 by 800, those that begin with `compact` in one 400 by 800, and `compact-narrowest` in one 320 by 640 (the schema has no stage size yet). Test a window exactly 1024 wide (expanded) and 1023 (medium), 600 (medium) and 599 (compact); on the web, a window 1280 wide with the root font size doubled is medium.

behavior.text: WHEN the app shell first decides the window's class, and WHEN a change of the window's width changes it, THE app shell SHALL emit windowClassChange exactly once with the class, and SHALL make the present class known to everything it holds through the platform's own channel for inherited values, so that a component inside it can follow the class without measuring the window itself. A change of width inside one class SHALL emit nothing.
behavior.verify: Test: a shell created at 1280 emits one windowClassChange with expanded; resized to 1100 it emits nothing; resized to 500 it emits one with compact.

behavior.text: THE app shell SHALL choose how the navigation is presented from the window's class: WHILE the class is expanded, beside the main region in the form the navigation drawer's expanded gives it (the standard presentation, NVD-53: its full form, its collapsed form, or — for a drawer that has no collapsed form and whose expanded is false — no place at all); WHILE it is medium and what the navigation region holds has a collapsed form (a collapsible navigation drawer), as that collapsed form beside the main region, widening over the content WHILE navigationOpen is true (the column presentation); and otherwise with no place in the layout, presented over the content WHILE navigationOpen is true (the modal presentation). WHILE the header region holds something, the navigation presented over the content — in the column and in the modal presentation alike — SHALL be drawn inside the frame below the header, from the header's bottom edge (from the window's top edge WHILE a static header has scrolled out of view) to the window's bottom edge, and its scrim SHALL cover only that part of the frame, so that the header is never covered or dimmed (APS-7, APS-32); WHILE the header region is empty it SHALL be drawn as APS-34 says. A navigation drawer in the region SHALL be drawn in each presentation exactly as a responsive drawer draws it (NVD-53 to NVD-55), and the two SHALL never disagree, because comp.app-shell.breakpoint.medium and comp.app-shell.breakpoint.expanded and the two widths that drawer reads alias the same window classes of the system (sys.breakpoint.medium, sys.breakpoint.expanded). WHILE the presentation is modal and the region holds something that cannot present itself over the content THE app shell SHALL NOT show it, SHALL keep it from focus and from assistive technology, and in debug builds SHALL report that the navigation of a narrow window needs a navigation drawer.
behavior.verify: Test with a responsive, collapsible navigation drawer in the region: at 1280 it is standard and Tab leaves it; at 800 its column is 72 wide beside the main region; at 400 nothing of it is in the layout. With a drawer that is not collapsible, 800 is modal.

behavior.text: WHILE the navigation has a place in the layout THE app shell SHALL put it at the start edge of the row, as wide as what it holds draws itself (a navigation drawer's width in its present form) and never wider than the room the row leaves it — the window less the main region's least width (its start and end insets, APS-8, and sys.target.touch between them) and less the aside WHILE the aside stands beside the main region (APS-9: comp.app-shell.aside.width, or a side sheet's own width as it is drawn, APS-10) — even where what it holds asks for more (a navigation drawer's least width included, NVD-97), so that neither the main region nor the aside is pushed past the window's end and the page never scrolls sideways (WCAG 1.4.10); THE app shell SHALL give the main region all the room that is left, and SHALL add no padding, fill or edge to it. WHEN that room changes (the window's width, an aside added or removed, a side sheet sliding in or out) the navigation SHALL be held to it in every frame it is drawn, with no motion of its own beyond what changes the room. WHILE scroll is page THE app shell SHALL keep the navigation in view while the page scrolls — from below the header WHILE the header is sticky, else from the top of the window, to the window's bottom edge — and what it holds SHALL scroll inside that height by itself (NVD-61), never the page with it. WHEN the window's scrolling view is pulled past its start or its end (the platform's overscroll) the navigation SHALL stay where it is: only the page's content moves with the pull. WHILE a person changes the width of a navigation drawer the navigation holds (NVD-98 to NVD-101) THE app shell SHALL give the main region the room that is left in every frame the width changes, the main region moving with no motion of its own, and SHALL keep the reader at the same place in the main content as far as the new width allows, as APS-23 does when the class changes.
behavior.verify: Test under the default system at 1280, in either direction, with a resizable navigation drawer (its handle's target 36, the gutter 32, sys.target.touch 36): beside an aside 240 wide the drawer is never wider than 1280 − 240 − (36 + 36 + 32) = 936, and without one never wider than 1280 − 104 = 1176, whether its least width asks for more or a drag or End asks for more; at that width, and in every frame of a drag past it, the document is no wider than the window.

behavior.text: WHILE menuButtonPlacement is header and the navigation region holds a navigation drawer THE app shell SHALL show the menu button where the product put it in the header in every window class and every presentation, whether the navigation is open or not. WHILE menuButtonPlacement is drawer THE app shell SHALL show it only WHILE the presentation is modal: in the column and the standard presentations the drawer's own menu button (NVD-37) stands for it. WHILE the header region is empty THE app shell SHALL show the menu button of the menu-button slot as APS-34 says, whatever menuButtonPlacement says. WHILE the navigation region holds something other than a navigation drawer THE app shell SHALL show the menu button only WHILE the presentation is modal, where APS-4 reports it. WHILE the navigation region is empty, and wherever this sentence does not show it, THE app shell SHALL NOT show the menu button, SHALL keep it from focus and from assistive technology, and SHALL give its place to what is beside it. WHEN menuButtonPlacement names a value the app shell does not define it SHALL be treated as header. THE app shell SHALL NOT restyle the menu button: it SHALL render as the icon-only Button it is, from its own tokens, with its own press, focus ring and minimum target, and its glyph SHALL stay the same while the navigation is open — its expanded state, not its picture, tells that it is.
behavior.verify: The fixtures `compact` and `medium` draw the menu button at the start of the header; `expanded` draws none. In the column presentation the drawer's own first header button is its menu button (NVD-37).

behavior.text: WHEN the menu button is activated THE app shell SHALL ask the navigation drawer in the navigation region for what the drawer's own menu button asks (NVD-37), in every presentation: WHILE the presentation is standard, its other form (expanded true or false), which the drawer applies and reports with expandedChange; WHILE it is column or modal and navigationOpen is false, to open — THE app shell SHALL then emit navigationOpenChange exactly once with true and become open (by setting navigationOpen itself on the web, through its binding where navigationOpen is one, and by the product setting it elsewhere), and the drawer SHALL present itself over the content below the header (APS-4, NVD-19) — over the whole window WHILE the header region is empty (APS-34) — taking focus; and WHILE navigationOpen is true, to close (NVD-20). WHILE the navigation is open over the content below the header THE app shell SHALL keep the announcement and the header as they are — drawn, reachable by pointer and keyboard and exposed to assistive technology, never inert — and SHALL make every other region inert to pointer, touch, keyboard and assistive technology (the skip link, the main region, the aside, the footer and the navigation bar), keeping the page from scrolling under the scrim as a modal layer does (MDL-2). WHEN the open navigation begins to close (NVD-20, NVD-21) THE app shell SHALL at once emit navigationOpenChange exactly once with false, navigationOpen SHALL become false the same way, and the regions it made inert SHALL stop being inert; focus moves as NVD-22 says, to the menu button where the menu button opened the navigation; the drawer and its scrim then leave by their motion, and nothing SHALL change when that motion ends (NVD-22). THE app shell SHALL expose the menu button as expanded WHILE the navigation is open over the content, and in the standard presentation WHILE the drawer is expanded, and as collapsed otherwise, controlling the navigation. A change of the window's class SHALL NOT change navigationOpen, except that the navigation's coming to stand beside the content ends its presentation over the content (NVD-54): THE app shell SHALL then emit navigationOpenChange once with false.
behavior.verify: Test at 400 wide: activating the menu button opens the drawer with focus inside it and aria-expanded true on the button; Escape closes it, focus is on the menu button and one navigationOpenChange carried false. Opened at 400 and resized to 1280, the drawer is standard, nothing is inert and one navigationOpenChange carried false.

behavior.text: THE app shell SHALL inset the main region's content from the region's start and end by the gutter of the window's class — comp.app-shell.gutter.compact, comp.app-shell.gutter.medium or comp.app-shell.gutter.expanded — and from its top and bottom by comp.app-shell.main.padding-block. WHILE mainWidth is contained the content SHALL be no wider than comp.app-shell.main.max-width and SHALL be centred in the room the region has inside its gutters; WHILE mainWidth is full it SHALL take all of that room. THE main region SHALL never be wider than the room the row leaves it: content that cannot shrink (a table, a line of code) SHALL scroll inside its own box (PRS-15), and SHALL NOT widen the frame or make the page scroll sideways. WHILE the navigation region holds a navigation drawer that draws its resize handle beside its end edge (NVD-96) THE app shell SHALL inset the content of the main region, and of an aside stacked in its column, from the region's start by the greater of the gutter and the handle's target across that edge (sys.target.pointer for a fine pointer, sys.target.touch for touch or where the input type cannot be told, HDL-5), so that the target lies over that inset alone and a press meant for the main content never reaches the handle (WCAG 2.5.8); WHILE the drawer draws no handle (resizable false, or the drawer not beside the content) the gutter alone SHALL inset it.
behavior.verify: Under the default system at 1280 with a navigation 240 wide and no aside, a contained main region's content is 768 wide and centred in the 976 between the gutters of 32; at 400 it is 368 wide between gutters of 16. A table 2000 wide in the main region leaves the window's own width at 400. Test at 1280 with mainWidth full beside a resizable navigation drawer: the main content starts 36 from the drawer's end edge (the handle's target; the gutter is 32), and what `document.elementFromPoint` finds 1 inside the content's start is the main region, at the top, the middle and the bottom of the drawer's height; beside a drawer with resizable false it starts 32 from it, and the point 1 inside is the main region's too. Before the drawer is defined its stylesheet gives the main content the same inset.

behavior.text: WHILE the window's class is expanded THE app shell SHALL place the aside beside the main region at the end edge of the row, comp.app-shell.aside.width wide, its content inset by comp.app-shell.aside.padding-inline at the start and the end and by comp.app-shell.main.padding-block at the top and the bottom, so that its first line stands level with the main content's; WHILE scroll is page it SHALL keep the aside in view while the page scrolls, as APS-5 says of the navigation, and the aside SHALL scroll inside that height by itself when its content is taller, and SHALL stay where it is WHEN the window's scrolling view is pulled past its start or its end. WHILE the class is medium or compact THE app shell SHALL place the aside in the main region's column, with the main region's gutters and, WHILE mainWidth is contained, its width and centring: above the main content WHILE asideOrder is before and below it WHILE asideOrder is after, comp.app-shell.aside.gap from it, scrolling with it.
behavior.verify: `expanded` draws the aside 240 wide at the end edge; `medium` and `compact` draw it below the main content, `medium-aside-before` and `compact-aside-before` above it, 24 apart.

behavior.text: WHERE the aside holds a component that takes its own width in the layout and draws its own edge (a standard side sheet, SSH-1 and SSH-7) THE app shell SHALL give the aside that component's width in place of comp.app-shell.aside.width, SHALL add no inset to it and SHALL draw no edge beside it; WHERE it holds a component that presents itself over the content (a modal side sheet) the aside SHALL take no space in any class. THE app shell SHALL NOT change the variant of what the aside holds: a product that wants a sheet beside the content in an expanded window and over it in a narrower one sets the sheet's variant from windowClassChange.

WHILE scroll is page THE app shell SHALL place the footer after the row of the navigation, the main region and the aside, across the frame's whole width, so that it is reached at the end of the page and the navigation and the aside stop staying in view where it begins; WHILE scroll is main THE app shell SHALL keep the footer at the bottom of the frame, below the row and above the navigation bar, always in view. THE app shell SHALL inset the footer's content by the gutter of the window's class (APS-8) at the start and the end and by comp.app-shell.footer.padding-block at the top and the bottom, and SHALL lay out nothing inside it: the footer's columns, links and controls are the product's.

WHILE footerHidden is true THE app shell SHALL NOT show the footer, whatever the footer slot holds: the footer SHALL take no space, draw no line (APS-18), add no landmark (APS-21) and have no stop in focus order (APS-22), the regions beside it SHALL take its room, and WHILE scroll is page the navigation and the aside SHALL stay in view to the end of the page (APS-5, APS-9). WHILE footerHidden is false THE app shell SHALL show the footer exactly while the product fills the footer slot (APS-1, APS-11): it SHALL NOT draw a footer, or expose a content-information landmark, for a slot the product left unfilled. WHEN footerHidden changes THE app shell SHALL draw the new arrangement at once, without a motion of its own, SHALL keep what the footer slot holds as the product gave it, and IF keyboard focus is in the footer as it is hidden SHALL move focus to the main region.
behavior.verify: `expanded-footer-hidden` fills the footer slot and draws `expanded` without its footer: the navigation and the aside reach the bottom of the window and no hairline is drawn above where the footer was. With footerHidden true the accessibility tree has no content-information landmark and Tab goes from the last stop of the content to the navigation bar (or out of the frame).

behavior.text: THE app shell SHALL draw each region in a stacking order of its own, so that nothing a region holds — whatever level its own stacking order (a z-index) gives it — is drawn over another region: WHILE scroll is page THE app shell SHALL draw the header and the navigation bar over every other region, the footer included, while the page scrolls under them, and SHALL draw the footer over the navigation and the aside. WHILE the navigation is presented over the content below the header (APS-4, APS-7) THE app shell SHALL draw the navigation and its scrim over the main region, the aside, the footer and the navigation bar and under the announcement and the header, within the frame's own stacking order and not in the platform's layer for overlays, so that the header is never covered or dimmed. WHILE the skip link has keyboard focus THE app shell SHALL draw it over every region (APS-19). THE app shell SHALL itself be one stacking order within the page, so that no level of its parts competes with what the product draws outside the frame. What stands over the whole frame — a menu, a popover, a tooltip, a snackbar, a dialog, a sheet, a modal drawer the app shell does not hold — SHALL be drawn above it by the platform's own layer for overlays, never by a level within a region.
behavior.verify: On the web, in an expanded window with the header sticky: a Code block (its copy button stands over its corner at a z-index of 1) and an element of the product's with `position: relative; z-index: 10`, each scrolled half under the header, and a footer taller than the window scrolled under it — at every point inside the header `document.elementFromPoint` is the header or inside it. In a compact window the same element scrolled under the navigation bar is under the bar. `isolation` is `isolate` on the frame and on each region, and the header's and the bar's z-index is greater than the footer's.

behavior.text: WHILE the announcement region holds something THE app shell SHALL place it across the frame's whole width above the header, with no inset of its own, in every class; WHILE scroll is page the announcement SHALL scroll away with the page and a sticky header SHALL then rest at the top of the window, and WHILE scroll is main it SHALL stay above the header. WHEN what the announcement holds is removed or closes (a callout whose open becomes false) THE app shell SHALL give its room back at once.

WHILE the window's class is compact and the navigation-bar region holds something THE app shell SHALL keep it at the bottom edge of the window across the frame's whole width, over the bottom system inset as the bar itself lays out (NVB-18), in view while the page scrolls, and SHALL end the page, or the frame, above it so that nothing is covered by it; WHILE the class is medium or expanded THE app shell SHALL NOT show the navigation-bar region, SHALL keep it from focus and from assistive technology, and SHALL give it no space. THE app shell SHALL NOT choose between the bar and the navigation for the product: a product whose bar is its navigation in a compact window gives no menu button.

WHILE scroll is page THE app shell SHALL be at least as tall as the window and as tall as its content, SHALL let the window's own scrolling view scroll the page, and SHALL make no region a scrolling view except the navigation and the aside where APS-5 and APS-9 keep them in view; so that the platform's find-in-page, a link to a place in the page, the return to where the reader was, and a browser's collapsing bars work as they do on a page without a shell.

WHILE scroll is main THE app shell SHALL be exactly as tall as the window, less the on-screen keyboard where one covers it, SHALL keep the announcement, the header, the footer and the navigation bar in place, and SHALL make the main region the one scrolling view of the frame, reachable and scrollable from the keyboard, with the aside scrolling inside its own height WHILE it is beside the main region and with the main region WHILE it is above or below it. THE window itself SHALL NOT scroll.

WHILE scroll is page and headerPosition is sticky THE app shell SHALL keep the header at the top of the window, above the main region, the navigation and the aside, while the page scrolls under it, and SHALL keep it there WHEN the window's scrolling view is pulled past its start or its end (the platform's overscroll): the content moves with the pull and the header does not; WHILE headerPosition is static the header SHALL scroll away with the page. THE app shell SHALL NOT fill, raise or edge the header: an app bar in it draws its own scrolled condition from the scrolling view it is connected to (APB-9), which is the window WHILE scroll is page and the main region WHILE scroll is main.

THE app shell SHALL hold the height of what it keeps over the top of the scrolling view — a sticky header's present height, measured again whenever the header changes size, and nothing WHILE headerPosition is static — and SHALL make it known to the scrolling view and to everything it holds, so that a heading or any other place a link or the address moves the view to (PRS-23), and an element that takes keyboard focus, come to rest below the header and never under it; likewise for the navigation bar's height at the bottom. A heading's own space before it (PRS-6) is added to that distance by the prose, not by the shell.
behavior.verify: Test at 1280 with a small app bar as the header: following a link to a heading in the middle of a long page leaves the heading's top 64 plus its own space below the top of the window; Tab to a link that is under the header scrolls it out from under it. With text enlarged so the bar is 80 high, the distance is 80.

behavior.text: WHILE separation is auto THE app shell SHALL part its regions as comp.app-shell.separation names, and WHILE separation is divider or gap as that value says, whatever the token says: divider draws a line comp.app-shell.outline.width thick in comp.app-shell.outline.color along the footer's top edge, along the start edge of an aside that stands beside the main region, and between the main content and an aside that stands above or below it, in the middle of comp.app-shell.aside.gap; gap draws no line and leaves the same spaces. The lines SHALL take no room of their own. THE app shell SHALL draw no line beside a region whose component draws its own edge (APS-10, APS-16) and none around the navigation, the announcement or the navigation bar. WHEN separation names a value the app shell does not define it SHALL be treated as auto.
behavior.verify: `expanded` follows the system (a hairline above the footer and at the aside's start edge under the default system); `expanded-divider` and `expanded-gap` draw the same under every design system.

behavior.text: WHILE the skip-link region holds a Link THE app shell SHALL make it the first element the keyboard reaches in the frame, before the announcement and the header, SHALL draw nothing of it while it does not have keyboard focus and still keep it in the focus order and exposed to assistive technology, and WHILE it has keyboard focus SHALL draw it comp.app-shell.skip-link.offset from the top and the start edges of the window, inside the system insets, above every region and every sticky part: in a box filled with comp.app-shell.skip-link.container.color and raised by comp.app-shell.skip-link.container.elevation, with corners comp.app-shell.skip-link.container.shape eased by sys.shape.corner-smoothing, padded by comp.app-shell.skip-link.container.padding-inline and comp.app-shell.skip-link.container.padding-block, its text in comp.app-shell.skip-link.label.typescale; the Link SHALL keep its own color, underline, focus ring and states (LNK-1). The box SHALL appear and go at once, without motion, and SHALL move no other part of the frame.

WHEN the skip link is followed THE app shell SHALL move keyboard focus to the main region itself — not to the first control in it — and bring the region's top into view below the header (APS-17) at once, without a scrolling motion, so that the next Tab reaches the first focusable element of the content and a screen reader starts reading there; the main region SHALL take focus only this way and SHALL NOT be a stop of the Tab order.
behavior.verify: Test: from a fresh page, Tab then Enter leaves `document.activeElement` on the main element; the next Tab lands on the first link inside it; Shift+Tab from there returns to the last focusable element before the main region, not to the region.

behavior.text: THE app shell SHALL expose each filled region as the landmark it is: the header as the page's banner, the navigation and the navigation bar as what they hold expose (a navigation landmark named by its own label), the main region as the page's one main landmark, the aside as a complementary landmark named by asideLabel (or by what it holds, where that names itself), and the footer as the page's content information; the announcement, the skip link and the menu button of the menu-button slot SHALL add no landmark. IF the frame holds no main region, or more than one, or an aside that has no name, THE app shell SHALL still lay out what it holds, and in debug builds SHALL report it.

THE app shell SHALL NOT be focusable and SHALL move focus through its regions in reading order, the same in every class and in either layout direction: the skip link, the announcement, the header (WHILE it is empty, the menu button of the menu-button slot, APS-34), the navigation, the aside WHILE asideOrder is before, the main region's content, the aside WHILE asideOrder is after, the footer, the navigation bar. A region that is not shown (APS-4, APS-6, APS-13, APS-31), and WHILE the navigation is open over the content below the header a region the app shell makes inert (APS-7), SHALL have no stop in that order. THE app shell SHALL NOT keep focus inside any region: WHILE the navigation is open over the content below the header, Tab and Shift+Tab SHALL move through the announcement, the header and the navigation in that order and on to what the platform has beyond the frame, and never reach what lies under the scrim. Only an overlay that stands over the whole frame (APS-32) holds focus inside itself.

WHEN the window's class changes THE app shell SHALL draw the new arrangement of every region but the navigation at once, without a motion of its own, and SHALL let the navigation drawer move from its place in the old presentation to its place in the new one by the drawer's own motion (NVD-54), drawn over the main region where the two overlap while it moves; SHALL keep scroll, headerPosition, mainWidth, asideOrder, footerHidden, separation and menuButtonPlacement as they are, and navigationOpen as NVD-54 keeps the drawer's open (APS-7); SHALL keep the reader at the same place in the main content as far as the new arrangement allows; and IF keyboard focus is on something the new arrangement does not show (a navigation bar's destination, a menu button that menuButtonPlacement drawer hides) SHALL move it to the main region, unless the navigation it holds has already moved it (NVD-54). WHERE motion is reduced the navigation SHALL take its new place as MOT-6 says, its change of size at once.

WHERE the app shell is rendered before the window's width is known or before its own code runs (a page rendered on a server) THE app shell SHALL already be laid out for the window's class by the platform's layout alone — every region in its place, the regions that the class does not show taking no space, the skip link first and working — SHALL present nothing over the content, SHALL make nothing inert, and SHALL emit no event until the class is decided; its own code SHALL then add only what layout cannot: the events, the menu button's opening of the navigation, and the measured distance of APS-17, without moving anything that was already drawn. WHERE a navigation drawer in the navigation region is rendered before its own code runs THE app shell SHALL give it, in an expanded window, the place it will take once its code runs: its expanded width held as NVD-97 holds it (the width the product gave it, between its least and its greatest width); its collapsed column (comp.navigation-drawer.collapsed.container.width.regular, or .compact WHILE density is compact) WHILE it is collapsible and expanded is false or its variant is modal (NVD-30); and no space WHILE it is responsive, not collapsible and expanded is false.
behavior.verify: Test on the web: with scripts disabled the fixtures `expanded`, `medium` and `compact` are drawn as with scripts, and following the skip link moves focus to the main element. With scripts enabled, no layout shift is recorded when the element is defined. A drawer written folded (collapsible, regular and compact density), modal and collapsible, hidden (responsive, not collapsible), and at a width (inside, above and below its range) in an expanded window, and folded at a width in a medium one, is drawn before the drawer is defined where it stands once defined, and no layout shift is recorded when it is defined.

behavior.text: WHILE the text size is enlarged THE app shell SHALL keep its gutters and insets, let every region grow with its text, and SHALL need no scrolling in two directions at any width down to 320 points: in a compact window the frame is one column, the main region never narrower than the window less two gutters, and only a block that scrolls in its own box (APS-8) scrolls sideways. THE app shell SHALL NOT fix the height of any region.

WHERE the platform's forced-colors or increased-contrast mode replaces the product's colors THE app shell SHALL let the system's colors fill its frame, SHALL draw the lines of APS-18 in the system's text color WHILE they are drawn, and SHALL draw an edge comp.app-shell.outline.width thick in the system's text color around the skip link's box, because the mode removes the fill and the elevation that set it apart.

THE app shell SHALL extend its fill under every system inset (status bar, camera cutout, home indicator, window caption) and SHALL keep the main region's, the aside's and the footer's content inside the start, end and bottom insets; the header, the navigation and the navigation bar lay themselves out over the insets at their own edges (APB-10, NVD-25, NVB-18), and the app shell SHALL NOT inset them a second time.

THE app shell SHALL take its layout direction from where it is used — the direction of the nearest ancestor that sets one, and the platform's own where none does — and SHALL have no direction setting of its own; WHEN that direction changes while the app shell is shown THE app shell SHALL draw itself for the new direction at once, without a motion of its own, keeping the window's class, navigationOpen and the reader's place in the content. WHERE the layout direction is right-to-left the navigation SHALL stand at the right edge and the aside at the left, the skip link's box at the top right, the menu button where the header puts its start, and the lines of APS-18 on the mirrored edges; the order of APS-22 SHALL NOT change, and nothing a region holds SHALL be mirrored by the shell.
behavior.verify: `expanded-rtl` draws the navigation at the right and the aside at the left; `compact-rtl` draws the menu button at the right end of the header.

behavior.text: WHEN scroll, headerPosition, mainWidth or asideOrder names a value the app shell does not define THE app shell SHALL render with that prop's default, and in debug builds report the unknown value.

THE app shell SHALL NOT restyle, resize or re-order what the product puts in a region beyond the place and the insets this spec gives, SHALL NOT decide which page is shown, follow a link, load anything, remember anything beyond its own lifetime (which page, how far a region was scrolled, whether the navigation was collapsed, how wide a person made it) or set the document's title or language; and SHALL NOT scroll anything with motion: every movement it causes (APS-17, APS-20, APS-23) is at once, whether or not motion is reduced.

WHILE the navigation region holds a navigation drawer whose filterable is true and whose filterShortcut holds exactly one chord, and either the navigation's presentation is modal and navigationOpen is false or it is standard and the drawer is hidden (a drawer with no collapsed form whose expanded is false, NVD-53), WHEN the person presses that chord anywhere in the window — read as SRC-38 reads a chord and with its exceptions (a press something else has taken, a key repeating while held, an input-method composition and, for a chord without mod, ctrl or alt, focus in an element that takes text) — THE app shell SHALL keep the press from doing anything else, open the navigation as an activation of the menu button does (APS-7: navigationOpenChange with true; where the drawer is hidden beside the content, its expanded becoming true), and ask the drawer to focus its filter (NVD-88), so that focus is in the drawer's filter field once it is open. WHILE the drawer is shown — beside the main region, or as its column — the drawer answers the chord itself (NVD-87) and THE app shell SHALL NOT. THE app shell SHALL bind no other key for the navigation.
behavior.verify: In a 360-wide window, a shell whose navigation holds a filterable drawer with filterShortcut ["/"]: "/" with focus on the main region opens the navigation, emits navigationOpenChange with true once, and focus is in the drawer's filter field; "/" typed in a text field of the main region types "/".

behavior.text: WHILE the header region is empty THE app shell SHALL take the menu button from the menu-button slot and SHALL show it only WHILE the navigation's presentation is modal, as APS-6 shows the menu button WHILE menuButtonPlacement is drawer, whatever menuButtonPlacement says: in the column and the standard presentations the navigation stands at the start edge from the top of the frame, below the announcement, to the window's bottom edge (APS-5), and a navigation drawer's own menu button (NVD-37) stands for the shell's. WHILE it is shown THE app shell SHALL place the menu button alone in the header's place — below the announcement, at the start edge of the frame — inset from the top of that place and from the frame's start edge by the gutter of the window's class (APS-8) and kept inside the system insets, SHALL draw no band, fill, edge or elevation around it, and SHALL begin the main region and the aside below it. WHILE scroll is page THE app shell SHALL keep the menu button at the top of the window, the gutter from its top edge, while the page scrolls under it — once an announcement above it has scrolled away (APS-12) — whatever headerPosition says, SHALL draw it over every other region as it draws a sticky header (APS-32), and SHALL keep it where it is WHEN the window's scrolling view is pulled past its start or its end (the platform's overscroll): only the content moves with the pull. WHILE scroll is main it SHALL stay in its place above the main region. THE app shell SHALL hold the gutter above the menu button and its height as what it keeps over the top of the scrolling view, as APS-17 holds a sticky header's, so that an anchor's target and a focused element come to rest below it. The menu button SHALL add no landmark and no region (APS-21), SHALL be reached in the header's place in the order of APS-22, and SHALL keep its keys; activating it SHALL open and close the navigation as APS-7 says. WHILE the navigation is open over the content THE app shell SHALL let the navigation drawer present itself as it does outside a frame that has a header (NVD-19): over the whole window from its top edge to its bottom edge, its scrim over the menu button and every region, keeping focus inside it and making what lies behind it inert while it is open, and returning focus to the menu button when it closes (NVD-22). WHILE the header region holds something THE app shell SHALL NOT show what the menu-button slot holds, SHALL keep it from focus and from assistive technology, and in debug builds SHALL report that the menu button of a frame with a header belongs in the header.
behavior.verify: `compact-no-header` draws the menu button alone at the top start corner, 16 from the window's top and start edges, with no band and the main region below it; `expanded-no-header` draws the navigation from the window's top edge and no menu button. Test at 400 wide with a navigation drawer in the region and no header: the page scrolled by 600, the menu button's top is still 16 from the window's top and the button is what `document.elementFromPoint` finds at its centre; activating it opens the drawer from the window's top edge with focus inside it and aria-expanded true; Escape closes it and focus is on the menu button; the accessibility tree has no banner. At 1280 and at 800 with a collapsible drawer the menu button is not drawn and has no stop in focus order.

keyboard.action: Moves through the frame in reading order: the skip link, the announcement, the header (or, while the header region is empty, the menu button of the menu-button slot), the navigation, the main content and the aside in the order asideOrder gives, the footer, the navigation bar. The shell itself is not a stop. While the navigation is open over the content below the header, only the announcement, the header and the navigation have stops; in a frame without a header the open navigation is a modal drawer that keeps focus inside it.
Moves focus to the main region and brings its top into view below the header.

keyboard.keys: Enter or Space, on the menu button
keyboard.action: Opens the navigation over the content, below the header (over the whole window in a frame without a header, APS-34), and moves focus into it; while it is open, closes it. Where the navigation stands beside the content, expands or collapses it (shows or hides a drawer that has no collapsed form). Escape in the open navigation closes it and returns focus to the menu button (the navigation drawer's own keys).

keyboard.keys: / (a filterable drawer's chord, in a narrow window)
keyboard.action: Opens the navigation over the content and moves focus to the drawer's filter field (APS-33). Where the drawer is shown, the drawer answers it.

accessibility.labeling: The shell has no role and no name. Its regions are the page's landmarks: banner (the header), navigation (named by the label of the navigation drawer or the navigation bar it holds), main (exactly one, unnamed), complementary (the aside, named by asideLabel or by the side sheet's headline) and content information (the footer, while it is shown: an unfilled or hidden footer is no landmark). The skip link is named by its own text and the menu button by its label, both in the product's language: Tanrei ships no words.
notes: The shell takes no input: the skip link is a Link and the menu button an icon-only Button, and each meets the minimum target by its own spec (LNK-17, BTN-5).

The skip link is what lets a keyboard pass the header and the navigation in one step (WCAG 2.4.1); the landmarks let a screen reader do the same. Both are needed: a sighted keyboard user has no landmark list.
Focus is never hidden by the frame (WCAG 2.4.11): the scrolling view keeps the height of the sticky header and of the navigation bar clear when it brings a focused element into view (APS-17).

While the navigation is open over the content it is drawn below the header and stays the navigation landmark the expanded menu button controls; it is not a modal dialog, because the header stays usable and a dialog would tell assistive technology that everything else is inert. The regions under the scrim are made inert instead, so nothing that cannot be seen can be reached (the disclosure pattern for a site's navigation, with the covered content inert).

Reading order, focus order and the order of the markup are one order in every window class (APS-22), which is why the aside's place is a setting (asideOrder) and not something the layout rearranges by width.
Reflow (WCAG 1.4.10): at 320 points the frame is one column; the widths that decide the class grow with the text on the web (APS-2), so 200 % text in a 1280 window is laid out as a medium one.

A second navigation landmark is not an error: a navigation drawer, a navigation bar, breadcrumbs and a pagination each name themselves, and only one of the drawer and the bar is shown at a time unless the product keeps both.
On SwiftUI, Compose, Flutter and React Native there is no skip link: each platform's assistive technology moves between regions by its own gesture or rotor, and the shell marks the regions for it.

web.name: tanrei-app-shell

menu-button.name: tanrei-button
menu-button.notes: An icon-only `<tanrei-button>` anywhere inside the header region, marked with the `data-app-shell-menu` attribute: usually the app bar's `slot="navigation"` child. In a frame with no header region, the element's own child `<tanrei-button slot="menu-button">` (APS-34): the slot is its mark. The glyph is its content.

web.notes: An element and a stylesheet: `<tanrei-app-shell>` attaches no shadow root, and the package's `@tanrei/web/app-shell.css` lays out its light-DOM children from the element's name, its attributes and each child's `slot` attribute alone, so a page rendered on a server is laid out before the element is defined and with scripts off (APS-24). The regions are the product's own semantic elements: `<a class="tanrei-link" data-standalone slot="skip-link" href="#main">`, `<div slot="announcement">`, `<header slot="header">` around a `<tanrei-app-bar>`, `<tanrei-navigation-drawer slot="navigation" responsive>`, the one `<main id="main" tabindex="-1">` child without a `slot` (the default region), `<aside slot="aside" aria-label="…">`, `<footer slot="footer">` and `<tanrei-navigation-bar slot="navigation-bar">` (and, in a frame without a header, `<tanrei-button slot="menu-button">` in the header's place), written in the order of APS-22; the stylesheet places them on a grid by name and never reorders focus. Attributes: `scroll`, `header-position`, `main-width`, `aside-order`, `footer-hidden`, `separation`, `navigation-open`, `menu-button-placement`, `aside-label`. The window's class is chosen by `@media` conditions in `rem`; a custom property cannot stand in a media condition, so the generator writes the two widths into the stylesheet from the active system's tokens (one stylesheet per system that changes them). The menu button is shown at every width while `menu-button-placement` is `header` (the default) and the navigation region holds a `<tanrei-navigation-drawer>`; otherwise it is hidden by the same conditions, with `:has(> [slot="navigation"][collapsible])` telling the column presentation from the modal one. With no header region the menu button of the `menu-button` slot is shown by the same conditions as for `menu-button-placement="drawer"` (APS-34), stands in the header's grid row with `justify-self: start`, and is `position: sticky` at the class's gutter (plus `env(safe-area-inset-top)`) from the top, with a block-start margin of the same so that it rests where it sticks, at `z-index: 3` as the header; the element measures it and publishes that margin and its height as the scroll offset (APS-17). A `menu-button` child of a frame that has a header is `display: none`, and the element reports it in debug builds. The drawer of a frame without a header is not held by it (NVD-19): it is the top-layer modal `<dialog>` over the whole window. The parts that stay in view while the page scrolls — the header while `header-position` is `sticky`, the menu button of a frame without a header, the navigation and the aside — are `position: sticky`; the web does not yet follow the part of APS-5, APS-9, APS-16 and APS-34 that keeps them where they are when the document's scroller is pulled past an end: a browser moves a sticky box that is not stuck with the pull, and holds only a `position: fixed` one still, and the fixed boxes would need the header to rest below an announcement until the page has scrolled past it and the navigation and the aside to end where the footer begins, which takes positioning that follows the scroll (scroll-driven animations are not in every engine, and the element listens to no scroll). The frame and each region are `isolation: isolate` (APS-32); the footer and the navigation bar are `z-index: 1` (the bar comes after the footer, so over it), a navigation drawer that stands over the content — open over it below the header, closing, or moving to a new presentation (the drawer's `data-over` state attribute) — `2`, the header `3` and the focused skip link `4` — levels within the frame, which no z-index inside a region reaches; a navigation drawer that draws its resize handle carries the `data-resize` state attribute, and while the frame holds one (`:has()`, asked of the frame) the main region's start padding and a stacked aside's start margin are at least sys.target.pointer, or sys.target.touch under `(pointer: coarse)` — the drawer's own condition for its handle's target — and, before the drawer is defined, in an expanded window the stylesheet reads the same from its attributes alone (`resizable` not `"false"`, no `variant="modal"`, and not a responsive drawer that is not collapsible written `expanded="false"`) (APS-8, APS-24); the navigation and the aside are `align-self: start` with a maximum block size of the dynamic viewport height less the scroll offset and `overflow: auto` with `overscroll-behavior: contain`; once the element is defined, a non-passive `wheel` listener on each of them (on the navigation where it is not a navigation drawer, which keeps its own) cancels a wheel turned toward an end the region already stands at, since Gecko keeps to `contain` only within one wheel transaction and would give a wheel at the end after a pause to the page. `scroll="main"` makes the host `100dvh` high and the `<main>` the scroller. It does not yet follow the part of APS-15 that has an aside above or below the main region scroll with it: a stylesheet cannot make the `<main>` and its sibling `<aside slot="aside">` one scrolling view, and making the frame itself the scroller in that arrangement would take the scrolling view away from the `<main>` that the app bar's `scroll-target` (APS-16) and the skip link (APS-17, APS-20) name, and would need the announcement's and the navigation bar's heights before the element is defined (APS-24). Until it does, a product that uses `scroll="main"` and wants the aside to scroll with the content in a compact or medium window writes that content inside the `<main>` for those classes. The stylesheet defines `--tanrei-app-shell-scroll-offset` on the document's root (until the element is defined: the small app bar's height while the header is sticky, else 0) and sets the root's `scroll-padding-block-start` from it — or the main element's while `scroll` is `main`; once defined, the element measures the header with a `ResizeObserver` and rewrites the property. The product's own sticky parts (a table's header row) read the same property. `--tanrei-prose-scroll-offset` stays 0 inside a shell: the scroll padding already clears the header, and prose adds only a heading's own space. The upgraded element adds: the read-only `windowClass` property, reflected as the `data-window-class` state attribute, and `windowclasschange` with `detail.windowClass`, from two `matchMedia` listeners (no resize listener and no frame loop); the menu button's `click`, which asks the `<tanrei-navigation-drawer>` in the navigation region for what its own menu button asks (NVD-37) — its other form where it stands beside the content, `open` where it is a column or hidden, closing where it is open — sets `navigationOpen` from the drawer's `open`, follows that drawer's `close`, and writes `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` through the Button's element properties; `role` and `aria-label` on a region whose element does not already give the landmark (a `<tanrei-app-bar slot="header">` with no `<header>` around it; an aside without a name takes `aside-label`); `tabindex="-1"` on a `<main>` that lacks it; and the debug reports of APS-4, APS-21 and APS-29. It listens to nothing while no region needs it. With `scroll="main"` the product names the main element's id in the app bar's `scroll-target`. `footer-hidden` gives the footer region `display: none` from the stylesheet (with `!important`, so a product's own `display` on its `<footer>` cannot bring it back): it then has no box, no landmark and no focus stop, its measured height is 0, and the element moves focus that was inside it to the main region. The skip link is hidden with a clip, never `display: none`, and shown on `:focus-visible`; under `forced-colors: active` its box gains a `CanvasText` border. Insets are `env(safe-area-inset-*)`. A filterable drawer’s chord (APS-33): the element holds one `keydown` listener on the window while the navigation’s presentation is modal, `navigationOpen` is false and the drawer in the navigation region is `filterable` with exactly one chord in `filterShortcut` (read as the drawer reads it); the chord opens the navigation as the menu button does and then calls the drawer’s `focusFilter()`. The React wrapper renders the same light DOM on a server. The navigation open over the content (APS-4, APS-7): with a filled header, the drawer is not shown as a top-layer modal `<dialog>` but drawn in the frame's own stacking order, below the header and over every other region, with its scrim covering only the frame below the header; the element sets `inert` on the skip link, the `<main>`, the aside, the footer and the navigation bar while it is open, holds the page's scroll as a modal layer does, and removes both when closing begins. The drawer learns that it is held so from its parent (a `<tanrei-app-shell>` whose header slot is filled), with no attribute for the product to write. Before a `<tanrei-navigation-drawer>` in the navigation region is defined (APS-24), the stylesheet places it from its attributes alone, in `:not(:defined)` rules under the same `@media` conditions: `collapsible`, `expanded="false"`, `variant="modal"`, `density="compact"` and `responsive` choose its column, its width or no space, and its width beside the content is `--tanrei-navigation-drawer-width`, which the product writes beside `width` (a stylesheet cannot read a number attribute as a length in every engine), held between comp.navigation-drawer.container.min-width and .max-width; `min-width` and `max-width` are read once the drawer is defined.

swiftui.name: TanreiAppShell

menu-button.name: TanreiButton
menu-button.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` in the header, marked `.tanreiAppShellMenuButton()`; the shell reads the mark from the environment and hides the button outside the modal presentation.

swiftui.notes: `TanreiAppShell(scroll:, headerPosition:, mainWidth:, asideOrder:, isFooterHidden:, separation:, isNavigationPresented: Binding<Bool>, asideLabel:) { main } header: { … } navigation: { … } aside: { … } footer: { … } announcement: { … } navigationBar: { … }`. A layout of its own, not `NavigationSplitView`, whose column widths and collapsing cannot be set from the tokens. The window's class comes from the width of the scene (a `GeometryReader` at the root, in points; Dynamic Type does not change it) and is published as the environment value `\.tanreiWindowClass`, which a search or a side sheet inside the shell reads. `scroll: .page` is one `ScrollView` holding the announcement, the main content, a stacked aside and the footer, with the header in `.safeAreaInset(edge: .top)` and the navigation and the aside beside it; `.main` keeps the footer in `.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)`. The header's height is published as `\.tanreiAppShellScrollOffset` and applied as the scroll view's content margin, so `ScrollViewReader.scrollTo` rests below it. Regions are exposed with `accessibilityElement(children: .contain)` and one entry each in a custom rotor, the aside labelled by `asideLabel`. No skip link: VoiceOver's rotor and Full Keyboard Access's group navigation move between regions. The navigation open over the content is laid out by the shell itself below the header — not as `.sheet` or a full-screen overlay, which would cover the header's `.safeAreaInset(edge: .top)` — as a scrim and the drawer in a `ZStack` over the content area; the covered regions are `.accessibilityHidden(true)` and kept from focus while it is open, the header is untouched, and the drawer is a container named by its label, not `.isModal`, since the header stays reachable.

compose.name: TanreiAppShell

menu-button.name: TanreiButton
menu-button.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` in the header with `Modifier.tanreiAppShellMenuButton()`; the shell draws it only in the modal presentation.

compose.notes: `TanreiAppShell(navigationOpen, onNavigationOpenChange, modifier, scroll, headerPosition, mainWidth, asideOrder, footerHidden, separation, asideLabel, onWindowClassChange, announcement = {}, header = {}, navigation = {}, aside = {}, footer = {}, navigationBar = {}) { contentPadding -> main }`, in the manner of a scaffold with a custom `Layout`. The window's class comes from `LocalWindowInfo.current.containerSize` in dp and is provided as `LocalTanreiWindowClass`. `scroll = Page` nests the main content, a stacked aside and the footer in one vertical scroll with the header pinned through a nested-scroll connection; the measured header height is provided as `LocalTanreiAppShellScrollOffset` and as `contentPadding`. Regions are exposed with `Modifier.semantics { isTraversalGroup = true; paneTitle = … }`, the aside's from `asideLabel`. System insets through `WindowInsets.safeDrawing`. No skip link: TalkBack and keyboard traversal groups move between regions. Not `ModalNavigationDrawer`, whose scrim and sheet cover the top bar: the shell's `Layout` places the open drawer and a scrim in the content area below the header; the covered regions take `Modifier.semantics { hideFromAccessibility() }` and `focusProperties { canFocus = false }` while it is open, the header keeps its semantics and focus, and a `BackHandler` closes it.

flutter.name: TanreiAppShell

menu-button.name: TanreiButton
menu-button.notes: An icon-only `TanreiButton` wrapped in `TanreiAppShellMenuButton`, placed in the header; the wrapper builds nothing outside the modal presentation.

flutter.notes: `TanreiAppShell({ required Widget main, Widget? announcement, header, navigation, aside, footer, navigationBar, bool navigationOpen, bool footerHidden = false, ValueChanged<bool>? onNavigationOpenChanged, … })`, a widget of its own in the manner of a scaffold (`CustomMultiChildLayout`), not `Scaffold`, whose drawer and bar slots draw Material's own. The window's class comes from `MediaQuery.sizeOf(context).width` in logical pixels and is inherited as `TanreiWindowClass.of(context)`. `scroll: page` is a `CustomScrollView` with a pinned header sliver; the header's height is inherited as `TanreiAppShellScrollOffset.of(context)` and applied as scroll padding for `Scrollable.ensureVisible`. Regions are `Semantics(container: true, explicitChildNodes: true, label: …)` in a `FocusTraversalGroup` with an ordered policy (APS-22). Insets from `MediaQuery.viewPaddingOf`. No skip link, except on Flutter for the web, which is not a target of this package. Not `Scaffold.drawer`, which covers the app bar: the open drawer and a scrim stand in a `Stack` over the body below the header; the covered regions are wrapped in `ExcludeSemantics` and `ExcludeFocus` while it is open, the header is not, and a `PopScope` closes it on back.

react-native.name: AppShell

menu-button.name: Button
menu-button.notes: An icon-only `Button` element passed as `menuButton`; the shell hands it to the header through context (`useAppShellMenuButton()`) and renders it only in the modal presentation.

react-native.notes: `<AppShell navigationOpen onNavigationOpenChange header={…} navigation={…} aside={…} footer={…} footerHidden announcement={…} navigationBar={…} menuButton={…}>{main}</AppShell>`. The window's class comes from `useWindowDimensions().width` and is given by context (`useWindowClass()`). `scroll="page"` is one `ScrollView` with `stickyHeaderIndices` for the header; the header's height is measured with `onLayout` and given by context (`useAppShellScrollOffset()`). Regions carry `accessibilityRole` where the platform has one (`header`, `menu`, `summary`) and `accessibilityLabel`; the order of APS-22 is the order of the rendered views. Insets from the safe-area context the package already depends on. The layout direction is the app's. No skip link. The open drawer is an absolutely positioned view below the header's measured height with a pressable scrim over the rest; the covered regions take `importantForAccessibility="no-hide-descendants"` (Android) and `accessibilityElementsHidden` (iOS) while it is open — not `accessibilityViewIsModal`, which would hide the header too — and `BackHandler` closes it.
